option_relations.rationale: Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) is a broader category of neurodegenerative disorders, but the specific genetic mutation (TBK1) and the presence of motor neuron disease symptoms (dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue atrophy, pyramidal signs, EMG findings) point to a more specific diagnosis than just FTD.

Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis–Frontotemporal Dementia (ALS-FTD) is a broader diagnostic category that encompasses TBK1-associated ALS-FTD. The option does not specify the genetic cause, making it a supertype.

Frontotemporal lobar degeneration–motor neuron disease (FTLD-MND) is a broader diagnostic category that encompasses TBK1-associated ALS-FTD. The option does not specify the genetic cause, making it a supertype. ALS-FTD is a form of FTLD-MND.

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-frontotemporal dementia (ALS-FTD) spectrum disorder (TBK1-related) is clinically equivalent to TBK1-associated ALS-FTD, as both refer to the same specific genetic and clinical entity.
